newsitem.title: USA: Mass. House committee to take up $583 mln bond.
newsitem.headline: Mass. House committee to take up $583 mln bond.

text.p: The Massachusetts House Ways and Means Committee is expected to take action later Tuesday on a $583 million bond issue that would upgrade the state's courthouses.

The courthouse bond is expected to be among the first bills to hit the House floor when a formal session begins Wednesday. House Speaker Thomas Finneran, D-Boston, sent the measure to the Ways and Means Committee late Monday afternoon.

Finneran, who has promised to get a balanced budget out of the House by mid-April, and Senate President Thomas Birmingham, D-Middlesex, have apparently agreed with Gov. William Weld that the state's courthouses are in sad shape.
Both houses passed a courthouse bond bill last year, but could not agree on its final form before the session ended on July 31.
The last authorization for repairs and new construction was a $300 million issue approved in 1988.

Since Weld sent lawmakers an $18.2 billion budget for the coming fiscal year, the governor has also forwarded bills to lower the unemployment insurance rate companies pay and restoring a law that would protect employees who refuse to work on religious holidays.
